column3: The Hebrew introduces David’s words with “said”; BSB specifies “ordered” and adds “himself” to David’s following the bier.
The Hebrew says the king lifted his voice and wept; BSB renders this as “wept aloud.”
The Hebrew preserves bronze fetters and “sons of injustice”; BSB has “fettered” and “the wicked.”
The Hebrew explicitly names bread as what the people came to feed David. Its oath says “thus may God do to me, and thus may He add”; BSB makes punishment and severity explicit.
The Hebrew twice places the approval “in the eyes” of the people.
The Hebrew calls the group “all the people”; BSB specifies “all the troops.”
The Hebrew coordinates “a prince and a great one”; BSB combines them as “a great prince.”
The Hebrew joins weakness and anointing with “and”; BSB supplies the concessive “though.”
